_operation: Calendar events.watch (the watch response that creates a notification channel)
_why: P5-005 requires recorded wire fixtures. This is NOT a recorded provider response. It reproduces the `watch` response the Calendar push guide publishes for a successfully created notification channel.
_the_point_of_this_fixture: THE SAME QUANTITY IS ENCODED TWO DIFFERENT WAYS, AND ONLY ONE IS COMPARABLE TO A CLOCK. On a notification, the channel's expiry arrives in the `X-Goog-Channel-Expiration` HEADER as a human-readable date (`Tue, 19 Nov 2013 01:13:52 GMT`). In this `watch` RESPONSE it arrives as `expiration`, a JSON NUMBER of milliseconds (`1426325213000`). The header needs a calendar, a locale and a timezone to interpret; the number needs only a scale factor. A renewal decision can only be driven by the number, and the guide's own value is used here so the millisecond-to-nanosecond scaling is pinned against it rather than inspected. (The Gmail watch lease is a THIRD encoding: an epoch-millis STRING.)
_why_the_type_is_a_number: The push guide's request section calls `expiration` an "`expiration` property string set to a Unix timestamp (in milliseconds)", but the `events.watch` REFERENCE the guide links to types the response field `expiration | long` and describes it as "Date and time of notification channel expiration, expressed as a Unix timestamp, in milliseconds." The reference wins -- it is the schema for the method, and the guide uses the same "property string" phrasing for `params.ttl`, which the reference types `string`. So this parser reads a NUMBER and refuses a string BY NAME: a string here is one of the other two encodings, and accepting both would erase which document declares which form.
_resource_id_is_read: `resourceId` is what the `channels.stop` call needs -- the guide's stop example carries exactly `id` and `resourceId` -- so it is read here: that is what makes the stop call constructible.
_token_not_read: The response also echoes `token`, but the connector already holds the token it set, so reading it back would be a second source for a value it chose. `kind` and `resourceUri` are informational and nothing acts on them.
_sanitized: No real channel id, resource id, calendar id or token appears here; the values are the guide's own examples.
